newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe coup trial postponed for a week.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe coup trial postponed for a week.

text.p: A Zimbabwean court on Monday adjourned for a week the trial of opposition leader Ndabaningi Sithole on charges of plotting to assassinate President Robert Mugabe and overthrow his government.

Justice James Devittie said he would rule next Monday on Sithole's application that the trial be postponed because he had been given little time to prepare his defence. He also wants to challenge the constitutionality of one law under which he is charged.

Sithole's lawyer, Tendai Biti, told a Harare high court that he had only received final prosecution documents from the state last Wednesday, and the first lot on October 23 when the trial date had been set for November 4.
"There was no adequate time to prepare the defence case, and further more the information supplied is scanty. The state approach is unfair and unreasonable," he told a packed court.
"And we are asking the court to postpone the trial because it would be unfair at this stage," Biti said, asking the judge to order the state to provide adequate information to the defence.
State prosecutor Abel Gotora said the information supplied was sufficient, and accused the defence of employing delaying tactics.
Sithole, 77, is facing three charges -- possession of arms, involvement in acts of sabotage and terrorism and conspiracy to murder President Mugabe, his political rival for over 30 years.
Biti also asked the court to consolidate the charges into one of terrorism as its definition under Zimbabwean law included possession of arms, murder or conspiracy to kill.

He also argued that a law and order maintainance act under which Sithole was charged placed the burden of proof on the accused, contrary to the constitutional guarantee that an accused person was innocent until proven guilty.
Sithole was detained for two days a year ago over the allegations, but has been out on bail since.
He denies the charges and accuses Mugabe of framing him to settle a personal vendetta.
